arguments_kinds.any: the leading arguments listed (the error code) match verbatim, and exactly one more follows: free text (Python repr is never pinned)
arguments_kinds.exact: the decoded arguments, verbatim strings, as many as listed
arguments_kinds.json: each argument parsed as JSON and compared by value (separators and key order are free)
arguments_kinds.json_keys: per argument: a string matches verbatim; an object {key: type} means the argument is a JSON object with exactly these keys (plus the case extra_keys, when sent), each value of that type; a type is one of null, bool, int, float, str, list, object, or several joined by '|' (float|null)

cases.name: objects_lists_the_registry
cases.note: the Controller and the Mission, as every board registers them; device tasks join as they come up. Runs before any health: plan B registers the databoard on the first parameter read (health does one), and lists it from then on

cases.name: base64_bad_alphabet
cases.note: CPython's base64 is lenient: it drops the '@'s, the token decodes to '' and plan B answers 'no object ' instead of a parse error. The code is badargs either way; the Rust parser is strict and answers it as a parse error

cases.name: handler_exception_is_internal
cases.note: pins the envelope rule -- a handler that raises answers err internal and the link survives. The trigger is a plan B defect (a JSON number reaches Mission.update, which iterates it); the Rust board refuses properties that are not a JSON object instead

cases.name: inspect_named_only
cases.note: a key=value token is named, not positional, so the object is missing

cases.name: update_bad_json
cases.note: refused, not badargs: plan B parses the JSON inside the guard that turns a driver refusal (ValueError) into err refused, and a JSON decode error is a ValueError

cases.name: log_duration_negative
cases.note: int() takes the sign, and a window of 0 or less stops the tee

cases.name: log_duration_plus_sign
cases.note: opens a 5 ms window; the next two cases run inside it on the virtual clock

cases.name: log_duration_underscores
cases.note: int() accepts '1_000' on CPython and on the board alike (MicroPython's py/parsenum.c skips every '_'), so a port's duration parse must too. MicroPython also takes '_1000' and '1__000', which CPython refuses: this oracle cannot speak for them, so no case pins them

cases.name: log_stop_after_a_window
cases.note: returns what the window buffered (nothing: no request logs) and stops it

cases.name: tlm_window_at_the_ticks_range
cases.note: the longest window plan B can arm: 536870000 us is below the 2**29 us ticks_add accepts

cases.name: tlm_window_past_the_ticks_range
cases.note: plan B arms the window with time.ticks_add(now, ms * 1000), which raises OverflowError from 2**29 us (8.9 minutes) on, so a longer window answers err internal. The Rust board keeps its window in 64 bits and has no such limit

cases.name: tlm_duration_past_64_bits
cases.note: plan B takes any integer, then fails arming the window (err internal); the Rust board parses a 64-bit integer and refuses a longer one as badargs

cases.name: stage_hold_on_the_ground
cases.note: done is a ground stage, so nothing is gated, but the stage is held (manual)

cases.name: arm_refused_while_held
cases.note: a held stage is an arm problem on every board: err unsafe, the problems as JSON

expected: refused in flight -- stage is gliding (ground-only: setting/done)
cases.name: ground_only_refused_in_flight
cases.note: the gate text is verbatim: it starts with the word refused, but its code is unsafe

expected: refused -- stage is gliding (changes only in setting)

cases.name: update_while_held
cases.note: plan B leaves update open in every stage; the Rust board refuses every change outside SETTING (the operator's rule, doc/specs/avionics-port.md §6)

expected: refused -- stage is gliding (changes only in setting)

cases.name: stage_auto_releases_the_hold
cases.note: the stage stays where it was held; only the hold (manual) goes

cases.name: stage_setting_returns_to_the_ground
cases.note: a return to the ground, not a hold: manual stays false

cases.name: report
cases.note: the Controller runs no tasks here, and the Rust board none until its drivers are ported

cases.name: verify
cases.note: the shape only: which devices are up, and so pass and ready, depend on the hardware

cases.name: update_mission_sets_the_clock
cases.note: the hub syncs a cold board this way (one whose clock reads inside 2000, as this one did until here); epoch is listed whenever the RTC was set

cases.name: whoami
cases.note: boot_id is null when nothing counted the boot (an NVS failure)

cases.name: health
cases.note: temp is null when the die sensor fails. position and agl are always present: Databoard.parameter() creates the channel on first read, so they are null until fresh. launchpad is null with no launch point and no fix, site null with no site selected

cases.name: inspect_mission
cases.note: the HPRC default mission: launch point set and zone in range, so the geometry keys are present
